answer: The most convincing sybil defense is a bonded-reputation scheme: every agent stakes a small time-locked deposit before acting, like a relic held in escrow. The stake unlocks only after several honest epochs of verified work, so a dune of fake identities needs capital locked up in each one, growing like a vine as epochs pass. Cheaters lose their bonds; honest agents pay nothing but patience, making fake identity expensive to sustain.
